subject: Human digestive system
annotation_method: Manual experimental prompts and screening criteria; not a production plan or expert certification

cases.title: Whole system: flat educational illustration
cases.visual_message: The digestive tract is a connected route from mouth to anus, with distinct organs arranged inside the body.
cases.scene: A clear, colored, flat medical illustration of the human digestive system in an anterior torso cutaway. Show the mouth and a single esophagus descending into the stomach; liver on the patient's right, which is the viewer's left; stomach on the patient's left, which is the viewer's right. Show a small gallbladder beneath the liver and a pancreas behind the stomach in this transparent schematic view. Coiled small intestine occupies the central lower abdomen, surrounded by the thicker large intestine, continuing into the rectum and anus. Use the reference's organ arrangement. Distinct restrained colors, clean outlines, generous spacing, neutral pale background. The torso and organs alone form the finished artwork, with plain surrounding space for later composited labels.
checks: Liver and stomach occupy the correct anterior-view sides
A single esophagus reaches the stomach
Small intestine is central and large intestine frames it
The rectum and anus terminate the tract
Accessory organs remain distinct from the alimentary passage

cases.title: Whole system: dimensional torso cutaway
cases.reference_support: whole-organ layout; generated depth is inferred
cases.visual_message: Digestive organs fit together within the torso; their spatial arrangement remains consistent across visual styles.
cases.scene: A polished three-dimensional educational anatomical model of an adult torso viewed directly from the front, with a clean cutaway exposing the digestive organs. Preserve the organ positions and approximate proportions in the attached diagram. Liver occupies the patient's right upper abdomen, viewer's left; stomach occupies the patient's left upper abdomen, viewer's right. A single esophagus enters the stomach. A transparent portion of the stomach reveals the pancreas behind it; a small gallbladder sits beneath the liver. Central coiled small intestine is framed by the thicker colon and continues toward the rectum. Smooth matte organ surfaces, distinct natural colors, soft studio lighting, neutral pale background. Finished artwork consists of the anatomical model and plain background.
checks: Front view has correct left-right organ placement
Depth treatment does not swap or duplicate organs
Pancreas is behind the stomach in the stated transparent view
Small bowel lies within the colon frame
Digestive tract connections are visually coherent

cases.title: Accessory organs: close-up
cases.reference_support: organ identity and broad placement; fine duct routing is inferred
cases.visual_message: The liver, gallbladder and pancreas assist digestion by delivering secretions into the small intestine.
cases.scene: A focused, colored medical illustration of the upper abdominal digestive organs in an anterior transparent schematic view. Show liver on viewer's left, stomach on viewer's right, a small pear-shaped gallbladder tucked beneath the liver, and the elongated pancreas behind the stomach. Use transparency in the stomach wall to make the pancreas visible while preserving these spatial relationships. Depict the duodenum curving around the pancreatic head and simplified bile and pancreatic ducts entering the duodenum. Keep all organs clearly distinguishable and the duct paths continuous and easy to follow. Clean medical illustration, restrained colors, neutral pale background, plain surrounding space for compositor typography.
checks: Gallbladder is beneath the liver rather than an independent large organ
Pancreas has plausible elongated form and relationship to stomach
The duodenum relates to the pancreatic head
Ducts deliver into the duodenum rather than stomach or colon
Fine duct details absent from the overview reference are identified as inferred

cases.title: Stomach: longitudinal cutaway
cases.reference_support: organ silhouette only; internal wall and folds are inferred
cases.visual_message: The stomach is a muscular chamber that mixes food, with an inlet from the esophagus and an outlet into the small intestine.
cases.scene: An isolated enlarged human stomach shown as a clean longitudinal cutaway in a medical teaching illustration. Preserve its recognizable curved sac-like shape, with the esophagus entering the upper stomach and a narrowed pyloric outlet continuing into a short segment of duodenum. The near wall is cut away to reveal one continuous internal lumen, natural folded inner lining, and a visibly substantial muscular wall. A small amount of partly digested food sits within the lumen. Separate the external organ contour, cut wall and internal lining clearly through restrained colors and shading. Neutral pale background, uncluttered composition, plain surrounding space for later labels.
checks: Esophageal inlet and pyloric outlet are distinct and anatomically plausible
One lumen connects the inlet and outlet
Folds lie on the internal lining rather than outside the organ
Food is inside the lumen
Overview image cannot establish exact wall layers or microscopic accuracy

cases.title: Small intestine: wall cutaway
cases.reference_support: organ identity only; internal and microscopic structures are inferred
cases.visual_message: The small intestine's folded inner surface supports nutrient absorption while food travels through its lumen.
cases.scene: An enlarged isolated short segment of human small intestine shown in a longitudinal cutaway, in a clear medical teaching illustration. Reveal a continuous central lumen bordered by an inner mucosal surface with circular folds and many small finger-shaped villi. Keep the villi small relative to the bowel tube and projecting inward from the lining into the lumen. The outer wall shows a simple continuous muscular layer. A small amount of intestinal contents stays within the lumen. Use restrained contrasting colors to separate lumen, inner lining and outer muscular wall. Neutral pale background, clean composition, plain surrounding space for later explanatory graphics.
checks: The cutaway is a hollow intestinal tube with a continuous lumen
Folds and villi project inward from the lining
Villi are not external tentacles or large separate organs
Wall remains continuous around the lumen
Supplied whole-organ reference does not verify mucosal or histological detail

cases.title: Esophagus: peristalsis teaching frame
cases.reference_support: organ identity only; movement and cutaway anatomy are inferred
cases.visual_message: Peristalsis moves swallowed food along the esophagus through coordinated muscular contraction.
cases.scene: A simplified longitudinal cutaway of a short vertical segment of human esophagus, enlarged as a medical teaching frame. Show a single continuous muscular tube and one rounded food bolus in its lumen. The muscular wall narrows immediately above the bolus, illustrating contraction behind downward-moving food; the lumen immediately below the bolus is relaxed and open. Make the wall visibly continuous and the bolus clearly contained within the passage. Use distinct restrained colors for muscle and food, a neutral pale background, and plain surrounding space for later composited motion arrows and labels.
checks: A single food bolus remains inside a continuous esophageal lumen
Contraction is above and behind the descending bolus
The passage below the bolus is open
Image is an explanatory still rather than proof of a motion sequence
Whole-organ source image does not depict this dynamic mechanism
